description: Held-out check for gates.v3 (ADR-0042): 40 raw gen.v3 drafts for an accountant, sampled after the gates.v3 wording and thresholds were chosen on gates.v3.json and labelled before any gate saw them. Same label definitions as gates.v3.json.

items.prompt: At a new cafe, do you order your usual drink or try their signature specialty?
options: Your usual drink
Their signature specialty

items.prompt: You burn dinner while guests are arriving in 10 minutes. What do you do?
options: Panic and order takeout
Stay calm and salvage what you can

items.prompt: You're assembling furniture with vague instructions. How do you proceed?
options: Look up exact steps online
Figure it out as you go

items.prompt: Your neighbour wants to repaint their door a bright colour that clashes with the street's look. What do you think?
options: They should keep the street's style
They can paint it however they like

items.prompt: Your family always does Sunday lunch at 1pm. A relative suggests moving it to 3pm. How do you react?
options: Prefer to keep 1pm
Happy to shift to 3pm

items.prompt: You're in a queue and someone cuts in. What do you do?
options: Point out the queue
Let it go

items.prompt: You get a promotion at work. How do you tell your friends?
options: Wait until they ask
Call them right away with the news

items.prompt: You try a new sport and are the worst in the group. What's your next step?
options: Accept you're not naturally good
Keep practicing to improve

items.prompt: Your manager gives you a project in an unfamiliar area. What's your first thought?
options: I might not be able to learn this quickly
I can figure it out with effort

items.prompt: Your firm considers a new flexible schedule that breaks the old 9-5. What's your stance?
options: Prefer the old structure
Welcome the change

items.prompt: It's Sunday evening at home. How do you handle the week ahead?
options: I write out each day's tasks and appointments
I note the main things and keep the rest loose
I check Monday morning and take it from there
I don't plan — the week sorts itself out

items.prompt: It's 11pm and you're mid-episode, with the alarm set for 6:30.
options: Watch until the credits roll
One more episode, then bed
Watch 15 more minutes, then stop
Pause it now and go to bed
Phone's already charging in the kitchen, lights out at 10:30

items.prompt: A friend books a trip and the cheap fare is non-refundable and non-changeable. Do you take that fare?
options: Yes
No

items.prompt: You need new headphones. What actually happens?
options: I grab the first decent pair I see
I check a couple of reviews, then buy
I compare several models across shops before deciding
I keep researching for days to be sure it's the best one

items.prompt: A neighbour asks for help carrying boxes on your only free Saturday afternoon.
options: I say yes and give up the afternoon
I help for an hour, then head off
I suggest a shorter time that suits us both
I say I can't, my Saturday is mine

items.prompt: A friend asks you to sponsor their 10 km charity run for €20. Do you sponsor them?
options: Yes
No

items.prompt: A one-year move to another city appears: better pay, cheaper rent, but no guarantee it lasts. What do you do?
options: Take it — nothing here is worth missing it
Take it if I can keep a fallback here
Ask around first and decide slowly
Turn it down — too much could go wrong

items.prompt: A friend calls at 6pm: dinner in an hour?
options: Yes — I drop everything and go
Yes, if I can be ready in 20 minutes
I ask to push it to 8pm
I say another day suits me better
I decline — I need at least a day's notice

items.prompt: Two ways to reconcile a client's accounts, both correct: one is quicker, one is cleaner and takes an extra hour. Which do you use?
options: The quick one — it's correct, that's enough
Usually the quick one, clean version if time allows
The cleaner one, even if it runs late
I rebuild the working papers until the method is the best available

items.prompt: A client wants modest but steady growth. Do you steer them towards the option with bigger possible swings and bigger possible gains?
options: Yes
No

items.prompt: After a long week, friends invite you to a busy bar on Friday night. What do you do?
options: Go, stay late, and talk to people you've never met
Go for an hour, then head home
Suggest dinner at home with just one friend instead
Decline and spend the evening alone

items.prompt: You want a pair of trainers. They cost €90 today; a sale in three weeks brings them to €60.
options: Buy them today at €90
Wait three weeks and buy them at €60
Buy a cheaper used pair now instead

items.prompt: Your phone breaks and you need a replacement this week. How do you choose the new one?
options: Order the same model right away
Spend the evening comparing specs and reviews, then order
Ask three friends what they'd buy and take their pick
Walk into a shop and decide on the spot

items.prompt: Your family has held the same summer gathering, same place, same food, for fifteen years. A cousin suggests skipping it for a trip abroad instead.
options: Keep the gathering exactly as it has always been
Keep the gathering and do the trip another week
Try the trip this year and see how it feels
Drop the gathering for good and plan something new each year

items.prompt: Walking to a dinner reservation, you see a cyclist knocked off their bike just ahead of you.
options: Stop and stay with them until the ambulance takes over
Call 112 from the pavement and wait until help arrives
Call 112 as you keep walking, since others are already there
Keep going — enough people have stopped already

items.prompt: Your partner's elderly parent needs daily help for a month. It would mean giving up most weekends and your evening gym sessions.
options: Take on nearly all the daily shifts yourself
Split the shifts with relatives and keep some of your routine
Pay for a professional carer instead

items.prompt: After a big Sunday lunch with twelve relatives, you have the rest of the day free.
options: Nap and read at home alone
Meet one friend for a walk
Invite a few of them round for coffee
Head to a crowded market with whoever's keen

items.prompt: What does a weekday morning at home usually look like for you?
options: Same steps, same times, almost every day
Mostly fixed, but it drifts by half an hour or so
I decide each morning as it comes
No pattern at all from one day to the next

items.prompt: A client's receipts don't quite match their bank statement, and the filing deadline is Friday.
options: Reconcile every line before filing anything
File the solid figures and flag the gaps in a note
Send it back to the client to check and wait for Friday
Post the totals I trust and move on

items.prompt: Four client accounts to close, two weeks until the month-end deadline, and no one to delegate to.
options: Map out daily targets for all four today
Block the final four days and do them all then
Start with the biggest and take the rest as they come
Work through whatever looks most urgent each morning

items.prompt: A friend is late for dinner again. What do you do?
options: Say nothing, let it go
Make a light joke about it
Tell them directly it bothers you
Ask them to leave earlier next time

items.prompt: You bought a €80 concert ticket but can't go. Someone offers €40. What do you do?
options: Sell for €40 to recoup something
Give it to a friend
Go anyway even if inconvenient
Keep it and hope to use it later

items.prompt: A friend shares a news article with a surprising claim. What do you do?
options: Skim it and move on
Check the source and look for other coverage
Discuss it with friends to hear opinions
Ignore it

items.prompt: At a reunion, people ask what you've been up to. What do you highlight?
options: A recent promotion or award
A hobby you enjoy
Family news
Keep it general

items.prompt: You find a wallet with €50 and an ID on the street. What do you do?
options: Turn it in with all the money
Keep the money and turn in the wallet
Keep everything
Leave it

items.prompt: You're playing a board game with friends and notice you made an illegal move that gave you an advantage. What do you do?
options: Say nothing and continue
Admit it and fix the move
Blame the rules
Offer to skip your next turn

items.prompt: A neighbor lends you their ladder for a week. What do you do?
options: Return it with a thank-you note
Offer to help them with a task
Just return it
Forget to return it

items.prompt: A friend cancels plans at the last minute for the third time. What do you do?
options: Say nothing but feel annoyed
Tell them directly it bothers you
Ask if something is wrong
Stop making plans with them

items.prompt: You're an accountant preparing for month-end close. How do you approach it?
options: Start with a checklist and timeline
Dive in and handle tasks as they come
Wait for all data before starting
Ask a colleague to lead

items.prompt: You're reviewing a financial statement for errors. What do you focus on?
options: The overall totals and trends
Every line item and footnote
Only the items flagged by software
A quick scan
